newsitem.title: FRANCE: Clinton, Chirac discuss NATO dispute, Russia ties.
newsitem.headline: Clinton, Chirac discuss NATO dispute, Russia ties.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton called French President Jacques Chirac on Thursday to discuss NATO's relations with Russia and a dispute over the alliance's future command structure, the French leader's office said.
Spokeswoman Catherine Colonna said the 35-minute telephone call took place in an excellent atmosphere, with a constructive discussion of both issues.

"President Clinton has just called President Chirac to discuss the Atlantic Aliiance in its two major components: the prospects for enlargement and relations between the Alliance, Russia and Ukraine just before the president goes to Moscow, and the ongoing reform of the Alliance on which France and the United States now have a wide-ranging dialogue," Colonna said.
She said the two leaders had discussed both issues "in a constructive spirit" and agreed to remain in touch.

Chirac met Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma on Thursday in Paris and is due to become the first Western leader to see Russian President Boris Yeltsin since his bout of pneumonia when he lunches with him outside Moscow on Sunday.

The United States this week rejected French ideas for splitting NATO's southern command, which controls the Mediterranean, in a compromise over Paris' demand for a European to take over from a U.S. commander in Naples. French officials said there was still time to find a solution before a NATO summit in July, which was the deadline.
